10:50 – 11:10Claude Setup
▾

Get Claude Pro ready for business use in 20 minutes. Follow the steps below — by the end, Claude will know who you are, how you work, and what you expect from it.

1 · Download the Apps

Install Claude on your phone and desktop so it's always within reach. claude.ai/download

2 · Settings → Account

Tell Claude how you want it to behave across every conversation. Open Settings → Account, correct your name, and fill in Instructions for Claude:

  • Who you are — your name, role, business in 2–3 sentences
  • Your business — what you do, who you serve, what stage you're at
  • Tools you use — Notion, Canva, Zapier, whatever's in your stack
  • How you like to engage with Claude — direct, concise, push back when needed, no fluff
  • Your technical level — e.g. "non-technical but strategic; explain things like I'm a smart non-developer"

3 · Settings → Privacy

  • Claude has opt-in features to share your data to improve its models — double-check these are OFF if you'd prefer not to contribute
  • Turn off metadata sharing / "Help improve Claude"

4 · Settings → Capabilities

Review Capabilities and select your preferences. I have everything turned on except Allow Network Egress.

  • Artifacts → turn ON — Claude produces formatted documents, charts, and interactive outputs
  • File creation & code execution → turn ON — Claude can build and run things, not just write about them

5 · Settings → Memory

Memory lets Claude remember things across conversations so you don't have to repeat yourself. You can also import memory from other AI providers.

  • Allow Search & Reference → turn ON — Claude can look back at your past chats when it helps
  • Generate Memory → turn ON — Claude builds up what it knows about you and your work over time
  • Sensitive topics → leave OFF — keeps health, finances, and other personal details out of Claude's memory. Claude still remembers your work and preferences, and you can change this any time.
Memory Maintenance

As you use Claude, your memory is going to become clogged without dated content. Set a reminder once a month to go through your projects & memory files to delete what's no longer relevant and correct misinterpretations, so Claude responses stay aligned as you grow.

For a full list of the features and terms we covered, visit the Resources section.

11:15 – 11:30Prompting Deep Dive
▾

Four frameworks that make any prompt better — plus a meta-prompt for when you don't know how to start.

RTCF — Role, Task, Context, Format my favorite

RTCF Framework
Role: You are a [e.g. brand strategist, CFO, legal advisor]. Task: [What you need done — be specific]. Context: [Anything it needs to know — project files, website links, what's important or not]. Format: [What good output looks like — list, table, tone, length, etc.]

RTF — Role, Task, Format

RTF Framework
Role: You are a [specific expert/role relevant to your task]. Task: [Describe exactly what you need done — be specific]. Format: Please respond with [format: bullet list / numbered steps / table / short paragraph / etc.]

TAG — Task, Action, Goal

TAG Framework
Task: I need to [what you're working on]. Action: Please [specific action you want Claude to take]. Goal: The end goal is [what success looks like — who is this for, what should it accomplish].

DREAM — Define, Refine, Execute, Adjust, Maximize

DREAM Framework
Define: I need help with [task/problem]. Refine: More specifically, [add any constraints, audience, tone, or context]. Execute: Please [specific output you want — write, analyze, create, summarize, etc.]. Adjust: Avoid [anything you don't want — jargon, certain formats, specific approaches]. Maximize: The most important thing is [what matters most about the outcome].

ROTE — Role, Objective, Task, Expectations

ROTE Framework
Role: Act as a [relevant expert]. Objective: The goal is to [what you're trying to accomplish overall]. Task: Specifically, [what you need Claude to do right now]. Expectations: [Length, tone, format, anything you want more or less of].

Bonus: When You Don't Know Where to Start

Clarifying Questions Meta-Prompt
Before you start, ask me 3 clarifying questions that would help you give me a significantly better response on this task: [describe what you're trying to do in one sentence].

Tips that actually help

  1. One prompt = one task — don't pack multiple jobs into a single message
  2. Give context upfront — include everything it needs in the first message, not drip-fed across follow-ups
  3. Tell it what good looks like — specify format, tone, length, and any constraints before it starts
  4. Keep threads short — 10–20 responses max, then start a new thread; use handover files to carry context forward
  5. Edit the original prompt when something's off — don't resubmit the same prompt and hope for a different result
  6. Add "Ask me questions until you're 95% clear on the task" when building something complex
11:30 – 12:15Brand Project & Skill Files
▾

Follow these steps to build your brand skill file and set up your Claude Brand Project — so Claude always knows your voice, your audience, and your business.

Step 1 · Create a Brand Project

Click Projects → New and name it "Brand". This becomes your dedicated workspace for anything brand or content-related.

Step 2 · Gather Your Brand Assets

Copy the prompt below and paste it into a new chat inside your Brand Project — but don't hit enter yet. First, gather everything you want to feed Claude. The more you give it, the better the skill file.

Brand Skill Builder Prompt
Role: You are a brand strategist and copywriter who specializes in helping founders define their voice. Task: Help me build a skill file for my brand — a document I'll upload to Claude so it can write in my voice across all content. Context: I'll share my website, examples of my writing, brand assets, and any other materials I have ready. Ask me one category at a time and use my answers to build the file. Cover: my business and what I do, my ideal client, my communication style and tone, what to avoid, key messaging themes, and examples of language that does and doesn't sound like me. Format: Compile everything into a structured skill file with clearly labeled sections. Make it specific enough that Claude could write a caption, email, or proposal in my voice without me having to explain my brand again.
What to pull together before you start
  • ✦ Your website link
  • ✦ Pricing documents
  • ✦ Brand colors (hex codes), fonts, and logos
  • ✦ Social media captions or posts you love
  • ✦ Emails or newsletters
  • ✦ Brand guides
  • ✦ Pricing guides

Step 3 · Follow Claude's Lead

Once you hit send, Claude will guide you through a series of questions. Answer them and feed it the assets you gathered. The more specific you are, the better the output.

Step 4 · Audit Your Skill File

Open a new chat window within the Project and paste the prompt below with your skill file attached. Claude will flag anything vague, missing, or contradictory.

Skill Audit Prompt
Role: You are a brand strategist and editor who specializes in reviewing AI instruction files and conversion copy. Task: I've just created a brand skill file. Find it and audit it. Context: This skill file is the document I attach to Claude whenever I need branded content. I've built it based on my brand assets, writing examples, and answers to guided questions. I want it to be as sharp and specific as possible — not just for voice consistency, but for conversion. Audit for: - Messaging gaps (anything vague, contradictory, or missing entirely) - Conversion blind spots (is it clear what I do, who it's for, and why they should hire me?) - Audience clarity (does it name a specific person with specific problems, or is it generic?) - Offer & pricing language (is it confident and specific, or hedged and unclear?) - Voice consistency (does the tone hold up across all sections, or does it drift?) - Anything that sounds like every other business in my industry Format: For each issue found, tell me: (1) what the gap is, (2) why it matters, (3) a specific fix or question I should answer to resolve it. Then give me a revised version of the full skill file with your changes clearly marked. Be direct — I want to know what's actually missing, not what's working.

Step 5 · Make Adjustments

Incorporate Claude's suggestions into your skill file — or make a note to revisit it after the workshop. This is a living document; it gets better over time.

Step 6 · Upload Your Bonus Skill Files

Add these to your Brand Project or directly to your Skills folder (Customize → Skills). Download them below.

↓ Copy-Editing Skill  MD ↓ AI-Isms Skill  MD ↓ Sales Copy Skill  MD
  • ✦ Copy-Editing Skill — use this to proofread anything Claude creates
  • ✦ AI-Isms Skill — filters out AI-sounding language so your content reads human
  • ✦ Sales Copy Skill — a layered copywriting skill for writing anything sales-related in your business

1:30 – 2:15Daily Morning Debrief Build
▾

By the end of this session, you'll have a scheduled automation that pulls from your actual tools and delivers a focused briefing every morning — before you open your inbox.

1 · Add your Connectors

Go to Customize → Connectors, then add the tools you want Claude to pull from. Common choices: Google Calendar, Notion, Gmail, Slack.

2 · Set Connector permissions

Once added, click on Yours, then click on each connector and adjust which tools Claude is allowed to use. Be deliberate — only grant what you actually need.

3 · Make a Project

Projects → New → name it "Morning Debrief" → add a short description of your role and what matters most in your day. This gives Claude the context it needs to filter signal from noise.

4 · Create a Scheduled task

Open a new chat in the Project → paste the prompt below. Claude will walk you through setting the time. Customize the instructions to your unique setup.

Morning Debrief Prompt
Every morning, pull from [YOUR DATA SOURCES — e.g. Google Calendar, Notion, Gmail, Slack] and deliver a focused briefing that includes: - What's on my calendar today - My top 3 priorities (pulled from [YOUR TASK SOURCE — e.g. Notion, a tasks file]) - Any urgent emails or messages that need a response - One open question or intention to reflect on before I start work Keep it under 300 words. No fluff. Write it like a smart assistant who knows I'm busy.

5 · Follow Claude's lead

Claude will ask for anything it can't pull automatically.

Tips for your Morning Debrief

  • Use this project to adjust the instructions as needed
  • For builds like this, there are always a few rounds of iteration to get it exactly where you want it
  • Adjust it seasonally to prioritize certain habits or projects
2:15 – 3:15Carousel Maker
▾

By the end of this session, you'll have a branded Instagram carousel built on a Claude Design canvas, using your brand skill and your favorite carousel styles.

1 · Find your inspiration

Pick 2–3 carousel templates on Instagram or Canva that you love and save them. These become your visual reference — Claude will use them to understand the structure, vibe, and layout you're going for.

2 · Add a New Project

Projects → New → name it "Carousel Maker" → add a short description of what it's for. This keeps the carousel context separate so Claude doesn't mix it with other work.

3 · Add brand photo access (if needed)

On the right panel, under Context → click "+" → Choose Folder → select your brand photos folder. Skip this step if you're not using custom photos in your slides.

4 · Copy in the Carousel Maker Prompt

Open a new chat in the Project → paste the prompt below → attach your inspiration images and your brand skill. Claude will ask questions until it has what it needs.

Carousel Maker Prompt
You're my carousel designer. Help me build one Instagram carousel on a Claude Design canvas, sized 1080×1350, one slide per artboard, side by side. I've attached my brand skill and 2–3 inspiration images. Work in this order, and wait for my reply at each checkpoint: 1. READ FIRST. Study my brand skill (colors, fonts, voice, words I never use) and my inspiration images. Tell me in 3–4 lines what you see: the layout, the structure, the mood. Ask me to confirm before moving on. 2. INTERVIEW ME. Ask no more than 5 questions at a time, until you know: - The one idea this carousel teaches - Who it's for and what they're struggling with - What I want a viewer to do at the end (save, share, follow, book) - How many slides (default: 5 = cover, problem, how it works, what to do now, call to action) - Anything I want included or kept out, and whether to use photos from my connected folder 3. WRITE THE COPY BEFORE DESIGNING. Show me the words for every slide and wait for my approval. - Cover: the hook only, short and bold, no body text. - Content slides: a short heading plus 2–3 sentences. Lead with the point, not the setup. - Be specific. Name real tools, numbers and actions. Never invent statistics or quotes. - Follow my brand skill's voice and avoid every word it bans. 4. BUILD ON A DESIGN CANVAS. Use my brand colors and fonts exactly. Take the layout, spacing and mood from my inspiration images, but never copy one. Keep text large enough to read on a phone (body at least 32px) with strong contrast. Add a slide number and my handle on each slide, and a swipe cue on the cover. 5. HAND IT OVER. Tell me what I can edit by clicking directly on the canvas, and list any assumptions you made. Then offer to write the caption and hashtags. Don't skip the checkpoints. If something is unclear, ask.

5 · Follow Claude's lead

Claude will ask about slide count, content type, fonts, colors, and layout until it has enough to build. Answer honestly — the more specific you are, the less back-and-forth you'll need.

3:15 – 3:45Astro Bestie
▾

Build a Claude Project that acts as your personal spiritual business coach — one that knows your Human Design and astrology charts and gives you direct, action-oriented guidance.

Before You Start

Grab these before you open Claude
  • ✦ Your Human Design chart (from myhumandesign.com or any free resource)
  • ✦ Your astrology chart (from astro-seek.com). Scroll to the bottom of the page to the AI copy/paste section and copy in that data
  • ✦ Save them as PDFs or screenshots — you'll upload both to the project files

Step 1 · Make a Project

Go to Projects → New, name it "Astro Bestie", and add a short description so you remember what it's for.

Step 2 · Copy and Drop in the Project Instructions

Paste the prompt below into the Project Instructions field. Modify as needed — especially the section labeled WHAT'S IN THIS PROJECT.

Astro Bestie — Project Instructions
PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS — Spiritual Business Coach ROLE You are a spiritual business coach providing personalized business guidance through the lens of Human Design and Astrology. YOUR JOB Use the chart files uploaded to this project to give direct, action-oriented guidance. This is not a personality analysis. This is strategic coaching to help get unstuck and move forward. WHAT'S IN THIS PROJECT I've uploaded at least one chart — Human Design, Astrology, or both. Read those files before responding to any question. If a question falls outside what the charts cover, search trusted sources to fill the gap. HOW TO RESPOND * Ground every answer in the student's specific chart data — type, authority, profile, defined/undefined centers, gates, channels, or natal placements depending on what's available * Be direct. Tough love is welcome. Skip the affirmations * Lead with the insight, follow with the action. If there's nothing actionable, don't say it * When the charts don't have enough detail to answer precisely, say so and work with what's there — don't make up placements * One question at a time gets the best answer. Complex questions should be broken down WHAT I COULD ASK * Why does [pattern] keep showing up in my business? * What's my natural decision-making style and how do I use it? * Where is my energy best spent and what's draining me? * How should I be showing up publicly / building visibility? * What's blocking me from [specific goal]? * How do I price, position, or structure my offers around my design? * What does my chart say about [current challenge]? REMINDERS * The charts are the source of truth. Don't project generic HD or astrology tropes — read their chart * Shadow patterns are fair game. Name them plainly * If the student pushes back on an interpretation, check the chart again before conceding

Step 3 · Add Your Chart Files

In the project, click the Files section and upload your Human Design and/or astrology charts. Claude will read these every time you start a new conversation in this project.

Try It — Questions to Ask

Start a chat in your new Astro Bestie Project and try one of these:

  • Write me a marketing plan based on my chart
  • What are shadow areas that show up in sales cycles?
  • What gives me energy in my business?
  • Why does [pattern] keep showing up for me?

Terms

Claude-specific features and general AI terms — in plain language.

Claude Terms
▾
Chat
The standard Claude.ai interface. Great for Q&A, brainstorming, writing drafts, execution, longer workflows, and scheduled tasks. Previously, Chat and Cowork were separate tabs, but they have merged. Use with intention and review what it does, especially when you're getting started.
Code
Claude's ability to build and run code. Zero experience required. Describe what you need in plain language and Claude handles the rest.
Skills
Reusable instruction sets. Think of them as recipes for Claude. Write one once and Claude knows exactly how to handle that task type every time. Example: a brand voice skill that makes all your copy sound like you.
Projects
Persistent context folders, similar to Custom GPTs. Add your instructions, files, and tone guidelines once. Claude carries them into every conversation in that project. Use one project per major workflow or client.
Connectors / MCPs
Model Context Protocol, originated by Anthropic and now an open standard. Lets Claude connect directly to your tools (Gmail, Notion, Calendar) without needing API keys or developer setup. Set permissions deliberately. I always have Delete blocked.
Claude Design
Now part of Claude Chat, it lets you easily create branded content. It's capable, but it burns through tokens fast. On the Pro plan, one design session can eat a big chunk of your daily capacity. Save it for tasks where it's genuinely the right tool.
Scheduled Tasks
Automations that run on a set schedule without you triggering them. Example: a morning debrief that pulls your top priorities before you open your email.
Routines
Automated sequences where Claude takes a series of actions in order. Example: an end-of-week wrap-up that summarizes, drafts next week's focus, and files notes.
Memory
Lets Claude remember who you are and how you work across conversations, so you don't repeat yourself. Turn on both toggles in Settings → Memory, and review what it has saved from time to time.
Network Egress
A setting under Capabilities that lets Claude's code environment reach out to the internet. Convenient, but it opens a door to the outside, so it's worth leaving off unless you need it.
Artifacts
Formatted, downloadable outputs Claude produces: documents, charts, interactive tools, code files. Anything you want to save or share.
Docs & Slides
New beta features similar to Google Docs and Slides. They're helpful for drafting in Claude, and the outputs are stored under Artifacts, or you can export them and move them to Google Docs or your desktop.
Chrome Extension
Brings Claude into your browser so you can research, summarize, and draft without switching apps. Powerful, but treat it like giving someone access to everything you're browsing. Limit it to what it actually needs. Use cautiously.
Claude Models
Opus is the deep thinker. Best for strategic planning and complex analysis. It burns tokens at 3 to 5 times the rate of other models, so use it when depth really matters.

Sonnet is the creative workhorse and your best default for almost everything.

Haiku is faster and lighter. Good for quick lookups, simple reformatting, and high-volume tasks where speed matters more than depth.
Effort
Controls how much processing Claude applies before responding. Higher effort means more thorough but slower. You'll see this as a slider or option when working on longer tasks.
General AI Terms
▾
LLM
Large Language Model. The technology behind Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini, trained on massive amounts of text to understand and generate language.
AGI
Artificial General Intelligence. Theoretical AI that could match or exceed human intelligence across any task. Not here yet, but this is what most AI labs say they're building toward.
Prompt
The instruction or question you give an AI. Better context gets you better results. That's really all there is to it.
Context Window
How much text the model can hold in mind at once: your conversation, uploaded files, instructions, all of it. Start fresh conversations for new topics so you're not filling the window with irrelevant history.
Token
The unit AI models use to process text, roughly three-quarters of a word. Context windows, pricing, and usage limits are all measured in tokens.
API
Application Programming Interface. The technical bridge that lets developers connect AI models to other software. If someone says they're "using the API," they're building something on top of the model.
Hallucination
When AI confidently states something false. It's pattern-matching without knowing what it doesn't know, so it fills in gaps with whatever sounds right. Always verify facts that matter.
System Prompt
Hidden instructions that shape how an AI behaves before you say a word. Every chatbot, assistant, and AI product has one. Project instructions and skill files are essentially your personal system prompt.
Agent / Agentic
AI that takes sequences of actions: searching, clicking, writing, sending, not just answering questions. Longer workflows in Claude Chat are agentic. Treat them accordingly.
RAG
Retrieval-Augmented Generation. AI that searches a document library before answering, so responses come from your specific files rather than general training data. Useful for knowledge bases, SOPs, or client libraries.
Fine-tuning
Training a model on specific data to specialize it for a domain. Different from prompting. It changes the model itself, not just how you talk to it. Usually only relevant if you're building a product.
Automation
Using AI (or any tool) to handle a task without manual effort each time. Scheduled tasks, Zapier workflows, and recurring routines all count. Do the thinking once, then let it run.
Markdown
A lightweight formatting language Claude uses constantly. Asterisks make bold, hashes make headings, dashes make bullet points. You don't need to learn it, but knowing it exists explains why Claude's output sometimes looks like it has symbols in it.
Local AI
AI that runs entirely on your device rather than in the cloud. Nothing leaves your computer. Useful for sensitive data, though the models are generally smaller and less capable than cloud-based ones like Claude.
Prompt Frameworks
▾
RTCF Framework (Cheyanne's fav)
Role — Tell it what role to play (e.g. brand strategist, CFO, legal advisor)
Task — What it needs to do
Context — Anything it needs to know about what it needs to do
Format — How do you want the output? What does good look like?
RTF Framework
Role — Tell it what role to play
Task — What it needs to do
Format — How you want the output (bullets, email, spreadsheet)
Chain of Thought
A prompting technique where you ask Claude to "think step by step" before answering. It dramatically improves accuracy on complex tasks — Claude reasons through the problem rather than jumping to a conclusion.
